title: Before the story, a reminder: everything glorifies Him.
subtitle: The opening of the surah about the exile
then: Ibn Abbas called this {idea}the surah of Bani an-Nadir{/idea}, a tribe of Madinah whose story follows. Before a single event is told, it opens with praise. Ibn Kathir says everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah and affirms His Oneness, and He is {idea}Wise in what He decrees.{/idea}
now: You are about to read the news, or tell a story from your own life about something that went badly. Start where the surah starts. {idea}Whatever happened, He is Mighty and Wise.{/idea} The story makes more sense from there.
old: Big events are just people's power and plans playing out.
new: Every story happens inside a world that glorifies a Mighty, Wise Lord.
try: Before you check the news today, say subhan Allah once and remember Who is in charge.

title: They trusted their fortresses. Allah came from where they never expected.
subtitle: Walls that could not protect, a lesson for those who see
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Bani an-Nadir had a peace treaty with the Prophet ﷺ, then betrayed it and plotted against his life. {trap}They believed their forts would save them.{/trap} The Muslims did not think they would ever leave. They surrendered for safe passage, taking what their camels could carry. {idea}Take warning, O people of vision.{/idea}
now: The pension fund. The good postcode. The alarm system, the insurance policy, the job that feels unshakeable. {trap}All walls.{/trap} Good to have. But the verse says {idea}what you fear can arrive from a direction you never watched.{/idea}
old: With enough security around me, nothing can touch me.
new: No wall protects me from Allah. Only He keeps me safe.
try: Name one thing you rely on to feel safe. Thank Allah for it, then remind yourself it is His.

title: Exile was the lighter outcome.
subtitle: What was decreed, and what remains
then: The verse says that had Allah not decreed exile for them, {trap}He would have punished them in this world.{/trap} They were allowed to leave with their belongings. Yet the verse adds that the account of the Hereafter {idea}was still ahead of them.{/idea}
now: You did something wrong at work and only got a warning. Relief. You think the matter is closed. {idea}A lighter outcome here is a chance, not a verdict.{/idea} The real settling happens later, and you can still fix things before then.
old: If the consequences were light, the matter is finished.
new: A light consequence in this world is mercy and time to put things right.
try: Think of one mistake you got away with. Make it right with Allah or the person today.

title: This happened because they opposed Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
subtitle: The reason behind the outcome
then: The verse names the cause plainly. Ibn Kathir explains that they had made a treaty and then {trap}betrayed it{/trap}, contradicting the Messenger ﷺ. {idea}Whoever opposes Allah, Allah is severe in penalty.{/idea} The outcome came from what they chose.
now: When something falls apart, it is easy to blame timing, other people, bad luck. {idea}Sometimes the honest question is: did I go against what I knew Allah wanted?{/idea} Not to drown in guilt. To learn and turn back.
old: When things go wrong, it is always someone else's fault.
new: My own choices against what Allah wants have consequences I should look at honestly.
try: When something goes wrong today, ask one honest question about your own part in it.

title: Cut or left standing, it was by Allah's permission.
subtitle: The palm trees during the siege
then: During the siege, some of the palm trees of Bani an-Nadir were cut and others left. The verse settles the matter: {idea}both were by Allah's permission.{/idea} It was so {trap}He would disgrace the defiantly disobedient.{/trap}
now: You made a hard call by the book: you let go of a friendship that was pulling you down, or turned down money that was not clean. People question it. {idea}If it was for Allah and within His limits, you do not need everyone's approval.{/idea}
old: If people criticise my decision, I must have done something wrong.
new: What is done within Allah's permission does not need the crowd's approval.
try: Before one decision today, ask: does Allah permit this? Then let that be enough.

title: Gained without a battle, so credit goes to Allah.
subtitle: What came without horses or camels

row.title: Allah gave it
sub: He is able to do all

then: Ibn Kathir explains that this property came {idea}without fighting, using neither horses nor camels{/idea}, since fear made them leave. Umar said the Prophet ﷺ took his family's expenses for a year from it, and {reward}used the rest for the community.{/reward}
now: The job offer that came through a friend you never asked. The refund you did not expect. {idea}No effort of yours, just a door that opened.{/idea} The verse teaches you to say: that was Allah, and to use it well.
old: Everything good I have came from my own hard work.
new: Some of my best blessings came with no effort at all. That is Allah's gift.
try: List one blessing that came to you without effort, and share some of it today.

title: So wealth does not just circle among the rich.
subtitle: Who the shared wealth was for
then: The verse lists who this wealth was for: relatives, orphans, the poor, the traveller. Ibn Kathir says it was spent this way {idea}so that it may not become a fortune passed among the rich.{/idea} Then a broad principle: {reward}what the Messenger ﷺ gives you, take; what he forbids, leave.{/reward}
now: The birthday gifts that only go to friends who will gift back. The dinner invitations that only go to people who can host you in return. {trap}Generosity that never leaves your own circle.{/trap} The verse wants it to reach the orphan and the traveller too.
old: I share mostly with people who share back with me.
new: Good wealth flows outward to people who cannot repay me.
try: Give something today to someone who could never return the favour.

title: They lost homes and wealth, and stayed truthful.
subtitle: The poor emigrants who left everything for Allah
then: The emigrants left Makkah, {trap}expelled from their homes and property.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they defied their people, seeking only Allah's pleasure. Allah calls them {reward}the truthful{/reward}, meaning truthful in word and deed.
now: You said Allah comes first. Then the job offer came with a condition that crossed a line, and you walked away. Your bank balance hurts. {reward}That is the kind of truthful this verse means.{/reward} Your words held when they cost you something.
old: Faith is mostly what I believe and say.
new: Truthful faith is when my choices back up my words, even at a cost.
try: Do one thing today that proves something you say you believe.

title: They gave others preference, even when they were in need.
subtitle: The Ansar, and the lamp turned off
then: The Ansar of Madinah {reward}loved those who emigrated to them{/reward} and felt no envy. Ibn Kathir reports an Ansari couple who hosted a hungry guest with only their children's meal. They put the children to sleep, turned off the lamp, and went to bed hungry. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}Allah wondered at what they did.{/idea}
now: Your flatmate's rent is short and you are tight too. Your sister needs a lift across town on your only day off. {reward}Giving when it pinches is the rank this verse praises.{/reward} And it adds: whoever is saved from their own greed has succeeded.
old: I will be generous once I have enough for myself.
new: Putting someone else first while I am in need is the highest generosity.
try: Give away one thing today that you actually wanted to keep.

title: Pray for those who came before you, and keep resentment out.
subtitle: The dua of the generations that followed
then: After the emigrants and the Ansar, the verse describes everyone who came later. Their mark is a dua: {reward}forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith{/reward}, and {idea}put no resentment in our hearts toward those who believe.{/idea}
now: The relative at the mosque with the views you cannot stand. The online argument with another Muslim that still annoys you. The verse hands you words for exactly this. {idea}Ask Allah to clean the bitterness out of your own heart.{/idea}
old: Some believers deserve my resentment for what they think or do.
new: I pray for believers before me and ask Allah to keep resentment out of my heart.
try: Say this dua today, thinking of one Muslim you feel bitter toward.

title: Big promises of support, and Allah testifies they are lies.
subtitle: We will stand with you no matter what
then: Ibn Kathir says Abdullah bin Ubayy and those like him {trap}sent a message to Bani an-Nadir promising them help.{/trap} The verse quotes their bold words, then says: {idea}Allah testifies that they are liars.{/idea} It was just words they never intended to keep.
now: I will always be there for you. Call me anytime. I have got your back. You say it at the party, and then the call comes at midnight and you let it ring. {idea}Allah is witness to the promises you make casually.{/idea}
old: Saying I have someone's back is just a kind thing to say.
new: A promise of support is a real commitment, and Allah witnesses it.
try: Only offer the help you will actually give today, and keep one promise you already made.

title: When it got real, they would not show up.
subtitle: Promises that vanish when tested

row.title: expelled?
sub: they will not leave with them

then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah foretold what would happen: the hypocrites {trap}would not fight alongside them, and even if they did, they would turn their backs.{/trap} He calls this verse {reward}good news for the believers{/reward}. The loud promises were empty.
now: The friend group who swore they would all stand up to the bully, then went silent when it mattered. The people who cheer you on online and disappear when you ask for help. {idea}Loud support is not the same as real support.{/idea}
old: The people who promise loudest will be there when I need them.
new: Promises are tested by hard moments. Allah's help is the one I can count on.
try: Show up for someone today in a quiet, practical way, without announcing it.

title: They feared people more than they feared Allah.
subtitle: When the wrong fear runs your life
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the hypocrites {trap}feared the believers more than they feared Allah{/trap}, citing another verse about people who fear men as they fear Allah or more. He calls this {reward}good news for the believers{/reward}. The cause: {idea}they are a people who do not understand.{/idea}
now: You would never skip prayer in front of your father. But alone in the hotel room, it is easy. You would never lie to your boss's face. But to Allah, quietly, you do. {idea}Notice whose eyes you actually feel on you.{/idea}
old: I behave well when people are watching. That is what matters.
new: The eyes that matter most are Allah's, and they are always on me.
try: Do one act today you only ever do in front of others, but this time alone.

title: They look united, but their hearts are divided.
subtitle: Togetherness on the outside, rivalry inside
then: Ibn Kathir explains they would only face the believers {trap}from behind fortified walls, out of fear.{/trap} Among themselves, the hostility was intense. {idea}You would think they were united, but their hearts are divided{/idea}, because they did not reason.
now: The family that smiles together in the Eid photo and does not speak once the camera is down. The team that shares the same logo and talks behind each other's backs. {idea}Real unity is in the hearts, not the group shot.{/idea}
old: As long as we look united, we are united.
new: Unity lives in hearts that want the same good, not in appearances.
try: Settle one quiet grudge with someone in your family or team today.

title: The same story had just happened, close by.
subtitle: A recent lesson they did not learn

row.title: it will not happen to me

then: Ibn Kathir says, according to Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ibn Ishaq, the people {idea}shortly before them{/idea} were the tribe of Bani Qaynuqa, who had already {trap}tasted the bad result of their conduct.{/trap} The lesson was recent and close, and still unheeded.
now: Your colleague got fired for cutting corners. Your cousin's marriage broke over hidden debts. You watched it happen, close up. {idea}The verse asks: did you learn, or are you walking the same road?{/idea}
old: Other people's mistakes have nothing to do with me.
new: When I see where a path led someone close to me, that is my warning too.
try: Think of one mistake you watched someone make. Check you are not doing a smaller version.

title: Shaytan says: do it. Then: I have nothing to do with you.
subtitle: The friend who disappears after the fall
then: Ibn Kathir says the hypocrites' broken promises to Bani an-Nadir were {trap}just like Shaytan{/trap}: he lures a person into disbelief, and once they obey, {trap}he disowns them{/trap} and declares himself free of their actions, saying he fears Allah.
now: The friend who said, just one drink, everyone does it, and then was nowhere when it went wrong. The voice in your head that says, go on, no one will know, and then leaves you alone with the guilt. {idea}Same pattern. Different costume.{/idea}
old: The ones pushing me to do wrong will be there with me afterwards.
new: Whoever pushes me toward wrong will abandon me once I fall.
try: Next time you hear go on, do it, pause and ask: who will stand with me after?

title: The tempter and the tempted end up in the same place.
subtitle: Disowning each other does not change the outcome
then: The parable ends soberly. Ibn Kathir says the end of both, {trap}Shaytan who commanded disbelief, and those who accepted his call{/trap}, is the same. {idea}This is the recompense of every unjust person.{/idea}
now: I only did it because they pressured me. The excuse feels solid. But the verse puts both people side by side. {idea}Pressure explains a choice. It does not erase it.{/idea} The good news: you can still choose differently today.
old: If someone else pushed me, the blame is mostly theirs.
new: I am responsible for what I choose, whoever pushed me toward it.
try: Own one choice today that you have been blaming on someone else.

title: Look at what you have sent ahead for tomorrow.
subtitle: The verse that filled two heaps of charity
then: Poor people from Mudar came to the Prophet ﷺ, and his face changed at their state. He recited this verse and urged giving, {reward}even half a date.{/reward} An Ansari brought a bag he could barely lift, others followed, and {reward}his face shone like gold.{/reward} Ibn Kathir: {idea}hold yourselves accountable before you are judged.{/idea}
now: Your bank app shows what you saved for next year. Your calendar shows what you planned for next month. {idea}What does your account for tomorrow, the real one, show?{/idea} Even half a date counts. And one person starting can move a whole room.
old: Tomorrow means next week's plans and next year's savings.
new: Tomorrow is the Day I meet Allah, and I am sending things there now.
try: Tonight, spend two minutes reviewing your day, and send one good deed ahead before sleep.

title: Forget Allah, and you end up forgetting yourself.
subtitle: What you lose when remembrance goes
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do not forget the remembrance of Allah, or He will make you forget the good deeds that would benefit you{/trap}, since recompense matches the action. He links it to another verse: {idea}let not your wealth or children divert you from His remembrance.{/idea}
now: Busy season at work. You stop reading Quran, then morning dhikr, then you are rushing prayers. A month later you barely recognise yourself: short-tempered, empty, scrolling at 2 a.m. {idea}Losing Allah is how you lose you.{/idea}
old: I am too busy for remembrance right now. I will come back to it.
new: When I let go of remembering Allah, I start losing myself too.
try: Set one fixed daily moment for dhikr, even one minute, and start it today.

title: The two outcomes are not equal.
subtitle: Paradise and the Fire are not the same ending

key.label: Does it matter how I live

then: Ibn Kathir explains these two groups are {idea}never the same in Allah's judgement{/idea}, citing verses that ask if those who do evil think they will be treated like those who believe and do good. {reward}Allah will honour the righteous.{/reward}
now: Some days it feels like it does not matter: the honest and the cheat both get the promotion, both buy the same car. {idea}The verse says the endings are not equal.{/idea} What you choose matters more than how the middle looks.
old: In the end, good and bad people all end up the same.
new: The ending is not the same. How I live decides which group I join.
try: Make one choice today because of where it leads, not how it looks now.

title: A mountain would crumble under this Quran. What about your heart?
subtitle: The weight of revelation

picture.label: If it came down on a mountain

then: Ibn Kathir asks: if a huge, hard mountain that understood the Quran would crumble from fear of Allah, {idea}why do your hearts not soften?{/idea} He recalls the tree trunk that {reward}wept like a child{/reward} when the Prophet ﷺ moved to a new minbar. Al-Hasan said: you are more worthy to miss him than the trunk.
now: You play recitation in the background while cooking, while driving, while answering emails. It is just sound. {idea}Words that would split a mountain, and you are half-listening.{/idea}
old: The Quran is something I listen to in the background.
new: These words could split a mountain. They deserve my full heart.
try: Listen to one page of Quran today doing nothing else, and let it reach you.

title: He knows the hidden and the seen, and He is merciful.
subtitle: Knowledge and mercy, side by side
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}knows all that we see and all we cannot, even ants in the darkness.{/idea} Then in the same verse: He is Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, {reward}owner of a mercy that embraces all creation{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: Someone who knew every secret of yours would be terrifying. Unless they were also the kindest being in existence. {reward}That is exactly who this verse describes.{/reward} Fully known, and still met with mercy.
old: Being completely known by Allah is something to fear.
new: The One who knows everything about me is also the Most Merciful.
try: Tell Allah one thing you are ashamed of, then ask for His mercy by name: Ya Rahman.

title: The King, the Pure, Peace, the Giver of safety.
subtitle: Eight names in one verse
then: Ibn Kathir explains each name. As-Salam: {idea}free from any defect.{/idea} Al-Mu'min: He gives His servants safety by promising He will never wrong them. He cites the hadith qudsi: {trap}might is My lower garment and pride My cloak; whoever disputes Me in either, I will punish.{/trap}
now: You feel unsafe, maybe in a new city, a new job, or a hard diagnosis. {idea}One of His names is Al-Mu'min, the One who gives safety and never wrongs you.{/idea} And when your ego swells after a win, remember who alone owns greatness.
old: I have to be the one in control and the one who looks great.
new: He is the King, the Giver of safety, and greatness belongs only to Him.
try: Pick one name from this verse and call on Allah by it in your next dua.

title: He measured you, brought you out, and shaped you.
subtitle: The Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner
then: The surah closes as it opened, with everything glorifying Him. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}Al-Khaliq measures and proportions; Al-Bari brings into being what He measured{/idea}; Al-Musawwir gives it its form. None but Allah can do all three. {reward}To Him belong the best names.{/reward}
now: You look in the mirror and list everything you would change. The verse says your measure, your existence and your form {idea}were each chosen by the Fashioner.{/idea} Whatever you work on, start from that.
old: I am just the sum of my flaws.
new: I was measured, brought into being, and shaped by the One with the best names.
try: Look in a mirror today and say: Ya Musawwir, thank You for shaping me.
